title: Artin-Rees lemma
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I\subseteq R$ an ideal, $M$ a finitely generated $R$-module and $N\subseteq M$ a submodule. Then there is an integer $c\ge0$ such that $I^nM\cap N=I^{n-c}(I^cM\cap N)$ for all $n\ge c$; in particular $I^nM\cap N\subseteq I^{n-c}N$ for all $n\ge c$, and the same holds for every $c'\ge c$ in place of $c$ (since $I^{n-c}N\subseteq I^{n-c'}N$).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00IN (lemma-Artin-Rees, line 12187); Stacks states c > 0, Mathlib gives c >= 0, and c may always be enlarged in the 'in particular' form used by Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 087X
